Build smart. Develop your military. Raid wisely. Save money. Grow gradually.

Don't worry about becoming powerful overnight. Good nations are built through consistent decisions over time.

— Rising Nations

mailLog.subject: Economic Tip
mailLog.message:
💰 RN ECONOMY TIP — Don't Spend Just Because You Can
One of the easiest mistakes for a new nation is spending every dollar as soon as it arrives.
Before buying something, ask yourself: “Does this purchase help me reach my next major goal?”
Saving your money allows you to make larger, more meaningful investments instead of constantly spending small amounts.
A nation that knows how to save can grow much faster than one that simply spends.

— Rising Nations

mailLog.subject: Rising Nations
mailLog.message:
🏙️ RN DEVELOPMENT TIP — Don't Rush Your Cities
More cities give you more capacity, but rushing city purchases can leave a young nation financially weak.
Your early development should focus on building a strong foundation before expanding aggressively.
Grow when you can afford to grow — not simply because you can.
A strong five-city nation is better positioned for future growth than a larger nation with no money and no military.

— Odyssey
The UN Secretary General
Union of Nations

mailLog.subject: RAID!
mailLog.message:
💰 RN ECONOMY TIP — Your Beginner Money Maker
For a small nation, one of the most practical ways to make money is raiding.
Instead of waiting for resource-producing improvements to slowly generate income, your military can actively generate money by attacking suitable inactive targets.
The basic cycle is: Build military → Find suitable targets → Raid → Collect loot → Save → Grow.
Your military can be an economic tool.

— Odyssey
The UN Secretary General
Union of Nations
